components.name: Checkbox
components.description: Row checkbox. WHY the shape: the 4px-radius square (radius/xs) is the only affordance that separates it from Radio's radius/full circle; the two must never be confusable, so the radius is never themed per surface. WHY the hit area: the visual box is 20x20, far under the 44px floor, so the whole row is the target - root frame min-height 44, full-width, and every adjacent row is separated by at least space/2 so no two 44px targets overlap (SS0.8). WHY the label association: the root frame IS the <label> element and Box is the visually-hidden native <input type=checkbox> rendered inside it, so association is implicit - no for/id pair, and clicking the Label text or the Description toggles the box. Checked/Indeterminate are discrete content states (a designer must place a pre-checked 'Save this address' row), so they are axes; Disabled is an axis because permission matrices and bulk-select headers need it. Hover/pressed/focus-visible stay interaction-only.

components.name: Checkbox/Bare
components.description: Label-less checkbox for DataTable row-select and bulk-select headers. WHY the shape: identical radius/xs square as Checkbox - a bare control has no text to disambiguate it, so the square is the ONLY affordance and must match the parent exactly. WHY the hit area: there is no row to click, so the component frame itself is 44x44 FIXED with the 20x20 Box centred - it needs no _hit44 helper because the frame already IS the 44px target, and in a 44px-tall table row the select target fills the row height exactly. WHY the label association: with no visible text there is no <label>, so the accessible name comes from the ariaLabel TEXT property on the 1x1 _aria-label layer, which maps to the aria-label attribute on the input (not a hidden span). Axes are identical to Checkbox so the same React component renders both.

components.name: Radio
components.description: Row radio for payment and delivery selection. WHY the shape: the 20px circle is radius/full and NOTHING else in the system that sits in a form row is - the circle means 'one of these', the Checkbox square means 'any of these', and because users scan shape before colour the two radii are fixed constants, never themed. The selected dot is a 10px filled circle inside a 1.5px brand-bordered 20px circle, never a 6px border, because a thick border animates badly and renders unevenly at 1.5x DPR. WHY the hit area: the visual dot is 20x20, so the whole row is the <label> - root min-height 44 and FILL width give a target of row-width x >=44 (SS8.8). WHY the label association: the root frame IS the <label> and Dot is the visually-hidden <input type=radio> inside it, so association is implicit; the GROUP name lives on a <fieldset>/<legend> wrapper (RadioGroup, a layout frame - not a variant set), and arrow keys move AND select natively. Selected/Disabled are the only axes: there is no indeterminate radio, and the group's error attaches to the fieldset, not to a row, which is why Error is not an axis here (see showMessage).

components.name: Radio/Card
components.description: Card-shaped radio for payment-method and delivery-method selection. A SEPARATE set, not a Style axis on Radio: a Style=Row|Card axis would change every geometry number per value, which is a different component wearing the same name. WHY the shape: the card is radius/lg (16) and carries the radius/full dot UNCHANGED inside it - the dot, not the card, is the affordance, so a user who has learnt the circle reads the card instantly; the card itself must never become square, because a square card plus a square mark would read as a multi-select tile. WHY the hit area: the whole card is the <label>, min-height 64 with space/4 padding on all sides, so the target clears 44 in both axes with room to spare, and focus-visible rings the WHOLE card (_focus at -4px, raw 20px radius) because the card IS the control - a ring on the 20px dot inside a 358px card would read as a stray artefact. WHY the label association: root frame = <label>, Dot = the visually-hidden <input type=radio>, implicit association; the group name is on the enclosing <fieldset>/<legend>. No Message layer and no error axis: a radio group's error attaches to the fieldset via aria-describedby (SS8.9), never to one card.

newTextStyles.name: Latin/Mobile/body-strong
newTextStyles.why: SS8.4 sends the SELECTED radio label to weight 600 - the one weight change in the primitive set, because a payment-method group is read at a glance. No existing style matches: Latin/Mobile/body is 15/400 and Latin/Mobile/button is 15/600 but at 120% line-height with 0.002em tracking, which breaks the 24px first-line box the dot's optical nudge is calculated against. Used by Radio and Radio/Card at Selected=True, Disabled=False.

newTextStyles.name: Bangla/Mobile/body-strong
newTextStyles.why: Bangla parallel of the above. 160% x 1.15 = 184%, tracking forced to 0 per the absolute Bangla tracking rule. Anek Bangla ships static 600 so this does not synthesise.

newTextStyles.name: Latin/Desktop/body-strong
newTextStyles.why: Desktop step of body-strong (body is 16px on desktop). Checkout radio groups render on desktop.

notes: MANIFEST CONVENTIONS - read before executing. (a) `layer` paths in `properties[].bindTo` are SLASH PATHS into the variant layer tree, not Figma layer names; the actual Figma layer name is the last path segment. `Mark/Check` and `Mark/Indeterminate` are the ONE exception: those are literal Figma layer names (they are siblings inside Box, not nested frames). (b) `cornerRadiusToken`, `padding`, `gap` hold a token NAME (string) when a variable exists, or a RAW NUMBER in px when it does not - a number means 'set the literal value, bind nothing'. (c) `minHeight` appears only on a variant's `frame` and maps to node.minHeight. (d) `fillToken: null` means no fill; `effectStyle: null` means no effect style. (e) `absolute.inset` is a single number applied to all four sides, with Ignore auto-layout ON. (f) `sizing.h/v` map to layoutSizingHorizontal/Vertical.

LABEL ASSOCIATION - the binding rule for all four sets. In `Checkbox`, `Radio` and `Radio/Card` the ROOT FRAME is the HTML <label> element and the `Box` / `Dot` frame is the visually-hidden native <input> rendered inside it (clip-rect technique, never display:none, which would drop it from the a11y tree and the tab order). Association is therefore IMPLICIT - no for/id pair is generated, and a tap anywhere on the row or card, including on `Description`, toggles the control. This is why the layers are named exactly `Box`, `Dot`, `Label`, `Description`, `Message`: Code Connect maps root->label, Box|Dot->input, Label->the label's text node, Message->the element referenced by aria-describedby. `Checkbox/Bare` has no <label> at all; its accessible name is the `ariaLabel` TEXT property on the 1x1 `_aria-label` layer, emitted as the aria-label ATTRIBUTE on the input. In a radio group the GROUP name is a real <legend> inside a <fieldset> (RadioGroup is a plain layout frame, never a variant set) and the group's error attaches to the fieldset via aria-describedby.

SHAPE AFFORDANCE IS LOAD-BEARING. Checkbox = `radius/xs` (4), Radio = `radius/full`. This overrides the spec's `radius/sm` (6) for the checkbox box: `radius/sm` is 8 in the live file, and an 8px radius on a 20px box is 40% of its width, which starts reading as a circle at 1x DPR - exactly the confusion the rule forbids. 4px keeps the corner unmistakably square. Consequence: the box `_focus` ring radius is host+4 = 8 = `radius/sm` (the spec said `radius/md`, which would be 12 on an 8px host and visibly rounder than the box it rings).

ERROR IS A BOOLEAN PROPERTY, NOT AN AXIS - and here is the mechanism. A Figma BOOLEAN can only drive `visible`, so it cannot repaint the Box border to `color/feedback/danger`. Rather than promote Error to a third axis (3x2x2 = 12 variants, 6 of them near-duplicates), `Checkbox` carries `_errorRing`: a 20x20 rectangle, absolute inset 0, fill none, stroke 1.5 `color/feedback/danger`, strokeAlign INSIDE, `radius/xs`, visible false. At inset 0 with INSIDE alignment it lands exactly on top of the Box's own 1.5px border and replaces it optically. The single `error` property binds to BOTH `_errorRing.visible` and `Message.visible`, which is legal - one property, many bound layers. `_errorRing` keeps its `_` prefix because it is never itself exposed as an instance property.

`error` is only meaningful at `Checked=False`. Per SS7.4 checking the box CLEARS the error, so code sets error=false on check; a designer who sets error=true on a Checked=True variant will get a danger ring over a brand-filled box, which is not a state the product can reach.

RADIO HAS NO `error` BOOLEAN - it has `showMessage` instead. SS8.2 inherits Checkbox's `error`, but SS8.9 is binding: a radio group's error attaches to the <fieldset> via aria-describedby, never to an individual input. So no row ever repaints its dot to danger, there is nothing for an `error` flag to recolour, and the only honest control is a visibility toggle on the `Message` layer for the one case that does exist - a designer placing the group-level message under the last option on a mockup board. `Radio/Card` drops `Message` entirely for the same reason.

PROPERTY DEFAULTS ARE GLOBAL, SO CONTENT THAT DIFFERS PER VARIANT IS NOT A PROPERTY. Every TEXT/BOOLEAN/INSTANCE_SWAP default here is identical across all variants of its set (the label string does not change when a box becomes checked), so the single-default rule costs nothing. The things that DO differ per variant - box fill, border, mark colour, mark visibility, label colour, label TEXT STYLE (400 vs 600 at Selected=True), card elevation - are baked into each variant's layers and are deliberately NOT properties.

SETTING A PROPERTY-BOUND `visible` REQUIRES setProperties ON AN INSTANCE. `focusVisible`, `error`, `showMessage`, `showLabel`, `showDescription` and `showTrailing` cannot be flipped by toggling the layer's eye on an instance - the lead must call instance.setProperties({ 'focusVisible#<id>': true }). Inside the main component the layer's own visibility is what the manifest states.

PHOSPHOR ICONS ARE FILLED PATHS - colour `Mark/Check` and `Message/Icon` with FILLS, never strokes. The spec's 'check icon stroke 2.25px' is void: there is no stroke to thicken. A filled Phosphor check at 14px already carries more mass than a 2.25px stroked check, so the spec's concern (a 14px check reading grey at 2x DPR) is answered by the fill, not by weight. `icon/check` is the checkmark glyph. For the indeterminate mark the manifest uses the spec's exact geometry - a 10x2 RECTANGLE at `radius/full` - because it is tokenisable and pixel-exact; there is no `minus-square` in the set, and `icon/minus` at 14px is the icon-instance fallback if the lead prefers an instance over a rectangle.

1.5px STROKES ARE UNBOUND RAW VALUES. `border-width/hairline` is 1 and `border-width/strong` is 2; the 1.5px control border the spec mandates for Box, Dot and the card has no variable. All `strokeWeight: 1.5` values in this manifest are literal. RECOMMENDATION for Foundations: add `border-width/control` = 1.5 and rebind these 20 strokes in one pass - 1.5 is the right value (1px disappears on a 20px box at 1x, 2px makes an unchecked box look pre-filled) and it should not stay hard-coded across four component sets.

RAW PX VALUES USED, WITH REASONS: Mark/Check 14x14 and Message/Icon 14x14 (between `size/icon-sm` 16 and nothing smaller; 16 inside a 20px box leaves a 2px inset and reads as a filled square); `Mark/Indeterminate` 10x2; `InnerDot` 10x10; `Radio/Card` `_focus` cornerRadius 20 (= `radius/lg` 16 + 4); `_aria-label` 1x1. Everything else is a token.

OPTICAL NUDGE: `BoxWrapper` / `DotWrapper` carry padding-top `space/0-5` (2px) so the 20px control centres on the 24px first line of `Latin/Mobile/body` (15 x 1.60 = 24; (24-20)/2 = 2). In CSS this is padding-top: calc((1lh - 20px) / 2), NOT a magic offset, so the Bangla build resolves it to 4px automatically (15 x 1.84 = 27.6; (27.6-20)/2 = 3.8 ~ 4). FOR THE BANGLA BOARD INSTANCES ONLY, override the wrapper padding-top to `space/1` (4). Both wrappers are FIXED 20 wide x HUG tall and must have Clip content = FALSE, as must `Box`, `Dot` and every root frame - the `_focus` ring sits 4px OUTSIDE its host and will be clipped away otherwise.

`_focus` LIVES INSIDE `Box` / `Dot`, not as its sibling. SS7.5 and SS8.6 draw it as a child of BoxWrapper/DotWrapper, but the wrapper is 20x22 (it carries the 2px nudge), so a -4px inset there would produce a 28x30 ring sitting 2px low on a 20x20 control. Parented to `Box` / `Dot` the -4 inset gives a true 28x28 ring concentric with the control, which is what SS7.4 actually asks for ('ring around the Box only'). `Radio/Card` is the exception: its `_focus` is a child of the ROOT frame at -4px, because there the card is the control.

HOVER IS A ROOT-FRAME FILL, NOT A SCRIM, FOR THE UNCHECKED ROW. Every root frame ships fill = none with `cornerRadiusToken: radius/md` already set, so :hover simply paints `color/bg/subtle` into an already-correctly-rounded box. Deliberately NOT `color/border/focus` - that token is reserved for focus so hovered and focused can never look identical. The `_scrim` layers (inside `Box`, inside `Dot`, and at card level) are the 8%/12% darkening for the CHECKED/SELECTED control and for the card, per SS0.2. All `_scrim` layers are instances of the shared `_scrim` helper component at LAYER OPACITY 0% - the layer schema has no opacity key, so set opacity on the instance; `visible: true` with 0% opacity is correct and intentional.

INTERACTION STATES, for the record, are not variants: hover = row/card fill `color/bg/subtle` at `radius/md` (unchecked) or `_scrim` 8% (checked/selected); pressed = Box scale(0.92) / InnerDot scale(0.85) over `fast` 120ms plus `_scrim` 12%; focus-visible = the `focusVisible` property. The check animates stroke-dashoffset full->0 over `fast` 120ms `decelerate` and the InnerDot enters scale(0->1) over the same; box fill crossfades 120ms. Reduced motion: both appear instantly. `spring` easing is forbidden.

BANGLA - WRAP, UNBOUNDED, for all four sets. `TextBlock` is FILL x HUG and `Label` / `Description` are FILL x HUG with wrapping on; truncation is forbidden everywhere. Root `minHeight` 44 (64 for the card) is a FLOOR, never a height - the row grows and the parent absorbs it. In `Radio` / `Radio/Card` the `TrailingSlot` is HUG x HUG and keeps its width; `TextBlock` is FILL and absorbs the loss, so a 40%-longer Bangla string wraps to 2-3 lines at 390px with the slot intact. Nothing is hard-coded per locale except the Bangla board's 4px wrapper nudge and the `Bangla/Mobile/*` style swap.

`TrailingSlot` NEEDS A PER-CHILD COUNTER-AXIS OVERRIDE. The root frames align children to START (Top) so the control sits on line 1, but the trailing slot must sit on the row's optical centre: set counterAxisAlignSelf = 'CENTER' on the `TrailingSlot` frame only (SS8.6 'counter align Center'). The layer schema has no alignSelf key - apply it in the API call.

`trailingSlot` DEFAULTS TO `icon/circle`, NOT `Price`. SS8.2 names `Price` as the default, but no Price component exists in the file yet, and SS0.9 forbids a blank-frame default because it hides layout bugs. The INSTANCE_SWAP therefore defaults to `icon/circle` at 20x20 (`size/icon-md`) per SS0.9's 'Lucide circle -> nearest Phosphor' mapping. ACTION FOR THE LEAD: once Tier 2 `Price` ships, repoint this default; the real payment group swaps in a logo row and the delivery group swaps in Price + ETA.

SELECTED + DISABLED LOSES WEIGHT 600 ON PURPOSE. SS8.4's and SS8.5's token tables mark (600) only on the `Selected=True, Disabled=False` row, so `Selected=True, Disabled=True` renders `Latin/Mobile/body` at 400 in `color/text/tertiary`. This follows SS0.4 - a disabled control must not look actionable, and that includes not looking emphatically chosen. FLAGGING IT: in a wholly disabled group this makes the selected option harder to spot. The adjacent explanatory text that says WHY the group is disabled is never tertiary; it is `color/text/secondary` or stronger.

DISABLED VARIANTS CARRY NO SHADOW AND NO RING. `Radio/Card` at `Selected=True, Disabled=True` has effectStyle null, not `Elevation/Light/e1` - per SS0.4 a disabled control gets no elevation. Elevation styles named here are the LIGHT set; the dark-mode board swaps `Elevation/Light/e1` for `Elevation/Dark/e1`, it is not a variant.

NO `_hit44` LAYER IS NEEDED BY ANY OF THESE FOUR SETS. `Checkbox` and `Radio` reach 44 through root minHeight plus a FILL-width row that is the whole label; `Checkbox/Bare` IS a 44x44 frame; `Radio/Card` is minHeight 64. The helper exists for controls whose visual box is under 44 with no row to grow into (Button Size=Small, IconButton Size=Small, Chip remove, Toast dismiss). Adjacent rows must still be separated by at least `space/2` (8) so no two 44px targets overlap - that spacing belongs to the enclosing group frame, not to these components.

COMPONENT-LEVEL WIDTH IS 358 (390 mobile viewport minus two 16px gutters) for `Checkbox`, `Radio` and `Radio/Card`. The root is FIXED at the component level because a top-level component cannot be FILL; every INSTANCE must be set to FILL horizontally. `Checkbox/Bare` is genuinely 44x44 FIXED and must never be stretched.

RESPONSIVE INSTANCE, NOT A VARIANT: under 480px with both a Description and a TrailingSlot, `Radio/Card` flips layoutMode to VERTICAL with the slot below the text at gap `space/2`. Build it on the documentation board as a detached-layout instance named `Radio/Card / narrow`. Do not add a Direction axis.

NUMERALS ARE WESTERN (0-9) IN BOTH LOCALES. Any digit entering `Label`, `Description`, `Message/Text` or a swapped `TrailingSlot` (a price, an ETA, '2-3 days') stays 0-9; the Bangla stack puts Hanken Grotesk first precisely so U+0030-0039 never resolve to Anek Bangla's Bengali numerals.

ACCESSIBILITY CARRY-OVER THE LEAD SHOULD HAND TO ENGINEERING: indeterminate is the DOM `indeterminate` property set in an effect, not an attribute, and aria-checked='mixed' is NOT added manually; a required terms checkbox is `required` + aria-required='true' with its error inline below the row and linked from the form summary; Tab enters a radio group at the selected option and leaves the group entirely (one tab stop per group) and arrow keys move AND select - do not intercept them.

SPACING TOKEN NAMES: the spec writes `spacing/N`; the live file has `space/N`. Every padding and gap in this manifest already uses the live `space/*` names. `space/0-5` is 2px, `space/1` is 4, `space/2` is 8, `space/3` is 12, `space/4` is 16.
